story.title: Thirteen People Killed in Tourist Plane Crash in Peru
story.summary: A small tourist plane crashed near Nazca, Peru, killing 13 people, including 11 passengers and two pilots. The aircraft was on a sightseeing flight over the Nazca Lines, a UNESCO-recognized archaeological site. The plane reportedly departed from the nearby city of Ica and crashed into a field approximately 4 miles from Nazca.

explore_lenses.label: Why do flights matter so much at Nazca?
explore_lenses.title: A core way visitors experience the site
explore_lenses.summary: The crash occurred on a form of tourism that Peru itself promotes as a distinctive way to see the geoglyphs. That makes the event relevant both to aviation safety and to access to a major protected cultural landscape.

claims.text: Peru's tourism ministry says visitors can use small aircraft to view the scale and legacy of the Nazca and Palpa Lines in a distinctive way.
The Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa are a UNESCO World Heritage site; UNESCO describes the geoglyphs as covering about 450 square kilometers of Peru's arid coastal plain.
Aerodiana, identified in reporting as the operator in this crash, says it has offered Nazca Lines overflights for 14 years using Cessna Grand Caravan aircraft.

explore_lenses.label: Have Nazca sightseeing flights had fatal crashes before?
explore_lenses.title: Two earlier deadly accidents are documented
explore_lenses.summary: This is not the first fatal aviation accident connected to Nazca sightseeing operations, though the earlier cases do not establish the cause of this crash or prove a common safety failure.

claims.text: Peru's transport ministry said seven people died when an Aerosantos Cessna 207 crashed near the María Reiche aerodrome shortly after takeoff on February 4, 2022; it referred the case to the CIAA, the aviation-accident investigation commission.
El País reported that a 2010 AriNasca aircraft crashed after completing its route, killing six people.
The CIAA's official archive lists a final report for the February 4, 2022 accident involving aircraft OB-2179, showing that prior accidents in the sector have been subject to formal investigation.

explore_lenses.label: Who will determine what caused this crash?
explore_lenses.title: Aviation investigators, with regulator support
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate cause remains unconfirmed. Peru's accident-investigation system, rather than initial witness accounts or operator statements, is the mechanism intended to establish findings.

claims.text: Peruvian authorities said the August 1 crash is under investigation; AP reported that Aerodiana was not immediately available for comment.
In the 2022 Nazca crash, Peru's transport ministry identified the CIAA as the competent body for accident response and investigation, while saying the DGAC would facilitate the inquiry.
The DGAC says it is responsible for regulating, overseeing, inspecting and sanctioning civil aviation activity, and for pursuing an acceptable level of operational safety.
The CIAA publicly maintains both provisional declarations and final reports for prior aviation events, including accidents and serious incidents.

story_report.summary: Thirteen people, including 11 passengers and two pilots, were killed when a small tourist plane crashed near Nazca, Peru, about 4 miles from the city. The aircraft had been conducting a sightseeing flight over the Nazca Lines, a major archaeological attraction viewed by visitors from the air. Peruvian authorities said the August 1 crash was under investigation, while the operator identified in reporting, Aerodiana, was not immediately available for comment.

sections.heading: Nazca Lines Depend on Aerial Viewing
sections.body: The Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa are a UNESCO World Heritage site spread across about 450 square kilometers of Peru's arid coastal plain. Peru's tourism ministry says small-aircraft flights offer visitors a distinctive way to see the scale and legacy of the Nazca and Palpa Lines. Aerodiana, identified in reporting as the crash operator, says it has provided Nazca Lines overflights for 14 years using Cessna Grand Caravan aircraft.

sections.heading: Previous Nazca Aviation Accidents Investigated
sections.body: Sightseeing aviation in the Nazca area has also seen previous fatal accidents. Peru's transport ministry said seven people died after an Aerosantos Cessna 207 crashed near the María Reiche aerodrome shortly after takeoff on February 4, 2022, and referred the case to the CIAA aviation-accident investigation commission. El País reported that six people were killed in a 2010 AriNasca crash after the aircraft completed its route; the CIAA archive includes a final report on the 2022 accident.

sections.heading: Peruvian Authorities Begin Crash Inquiry
sections.body: Authorities are investigating the August 1 crash. The CIAA maintains provisional declarations and final reports on aviation accidents and serious incidents, while the civil-aviation directorate, or DGAC, is responsible for regulating, overseeing and inspecting civil aviation activity and pursuing acceptable operational safety. In the 2022 Nazca crash, the transport ministry identified the CIAA as the competent investigative body and said the DGAC would facilitate the inquiry.

unresolved.text: The reviewed reporting and official sources had provided no preliminary finding on mechanical condition, weather, pilot actions, air-traffic issues or any other cause of the August 1 crash.
There was no confirmed indication in the reviewed reporting that the crash damaged the archaeological site or that sightseeing flights had been suspended.
The available sources do not establish whether earlier Nazca-area accidents involved causes, operating conditions, aircraft types or regulatory issues comparable to the August 1 crash.

related_stories.title: Infantino Halts Plan to Sell World Cup Profits Amid Widespread Opposition
related_stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has decided to abandon his controversial proposal to sell World Cup profits to private equity firms. This decision follows significant pushback from various stakeholders within the soccer community, reflecting widespread disapproval of the plan.

related_stories.title: UEFA Reacts to FIFA's Abandonment of World Cup Investment Plans
related_stories.summary: UEFA has expressed that FIFA President Gianni Infantino has lost their confidence following his decision to abandon plans to sell stakes in World Cup competitions to private investors. This move comes after significant backlash against the proposal, which aimed to create a commercial subsidiary for FIFA. UEFA called the abandonment a victory for the sport, while other soccer bodies, including those in Asia, have also voiced their opposition to Infantino's management style.

related_stories.title: Massive Pride Celebrations Across Europe Following Berlin Attack
related_stories.summary: Hundreds of thousands participated in Pride events across the UK and mainland Europe, following a deadly extremist attack at a Pride festival in Berlin the previous week. Major celebrations took place in cities like Hamburg and Amsterdam, showcasing solidarity and resilience in the LGBTQ+ community.
